summary: This project plan establishes a pragmatic path to launch a core customer support chatbot within a compressed two-week timeline using two software engineers. Due to the tight schedule and lack of an initial product owner and confirmed budget, enterprise SSO, multilingual support, and complex CRM integration are deferred to subsequent phases. The plan incorporates an illustrative engineering-only cost estimate, defines provisional task ownership, sets up a clear risk matrix, and establishes measurable acceptance gates replacing unrealistic zero-defect claims.

sections.heading: Executive Summary and Conflict Resolution
paragraphs: To deliver a functional chatbot within the compressed two-week timeframe using two software engineers, significant scope adjustments are required. The initial request to include enterprise SSO, multilingual support, CRM integration, and zero defects within ten working days creates a direct conflict with engineering capacity.

Consequently, enterprise features and integrations are deferred to Phase 2. The zero-defects requirement is replaced by a qualified quality gate. In the absence of a product owner and confirmed budget, senior stakeholders will provide daily prioritization sign-offs, and an illustrative engineering cost of INR 120000 has been established for baseline tracking.
bullets: Phase 1 Scope: Core chatbot functionality built by two engineers over 10 days.
Deferred Scope: Enterprise SSO, multilingual support, and CRM integration moved to Phase 2.
Governance: Stakeholders act as product owners to resolve requirement conflicts.

Stakeholder sign-off proxy & zero critical defects

sections.heading: Phased Scope and Timeline Plan
paragraphs: The project is structured into two distinct phases to reconcile the compressed two-week timeline and limited engineering capacity with the extensive feature requests. Phase 1 focuses exclusively on delivering a core customer support chatbot within ten working days using two assigned software engineers. Enterprise SSO, multilingual support, and CRM integration are deferred to Phase 2, which will commence post-launch upon budget confirmation and product owner assignment.

Phase 1 execution spans Weeks 1 and 2, covering core conversational flows, basic deployment, and user acceptance testing against a qualified defect threshold. Phase 2 schedule and resource allocations will be determined during post-launch reviews.
bullets: Phase 1 Week 1: Core chatbot logic, basic user interface, and initial integration testing.
Phase 1 Week 2: User acceptance testing, bug fixes for critical items, and production deployment.
Phase 2 Scope: Enterprise SSO integration, multilingual support expansion, and backend CRM integration.

tables.caption: Phased Scope and Timeline
rows: Core chatbot functionality and basic testing
Enterprise SSO, multilingual support, and CRM integration

sections.heading: Provisional Ownership and Risk Matrix
paragraphs: To ensure accountability during the compressed two-week delivery window, technical execution is assigned provisionally to the two software engineers. Engineer 1 acts as the Lead Developer responsible for core conversational logic and system stability. Engineer 2 acts as the Integration and Testing Developer responsible for user interface components and test execution. Stakeholders will jointly assume product owner duties for rapid sign-offs.

The risk matrix below outlines critical project risks, including timeline pressures and technical debt accumulation arising from the two-week constraint, along with corresponding mitigation strategies.
bullets: Engineer 1 Ownership: Core chatbot logic, architecture, and backend deployment.
Engineer 2 Ownership: User interface implementation, test suites, and bug triage.
Stakeholder Oversight: Acting product owner proxy for rapid scope decisions and daily reviews.

tables.caption: Project Risk Matrix
rows: Focus testing solely on core chatbot paths and defer advanced features to Phase 2
Schedule refactoring sprints during Phase 2 post-launch maintenance
Lack of dedicated product owner delays decisions
Designate a primary stakeholder proxy for daily 15-minute alignment sessions

sections.heading: Acceptance Criteria and Approval Gates
paragraphs: To ensure a realistic release under the two-week constraint, the unrealistic zero-defects requirement is replaced by a qualified acceptance gate. Phase 1 launch approval requires that there are no known critical or high severity defects in core chatbot flows during user acceptance testing. Minor defects will be triaged and addressed in Phase 2 post-launch maintenance.
Because there is no confirmed budget and no permanent product owner, key strategic decisions require formal sign-off from designated stakeholders acting as proxies before implementation proceeds.
bullets: Acceptance Gate: Zero critical or high severity defects in core user journeys.
Performance Criteria: Chatbot responds within three seconds under nominal load.
Approval Gate 1: Formal sign-off on Phase 1 core chatbot scope by Week 1, Day 3.
Approval Gate 2: Authorization of the illustrative engineering cost estimate of INR 120000 by Week 1, Day 5.
